subject.title: cron: ghost runs recorded as ok when gateway is down (durationMs < 50ms)

question: Should the fix for this issue be a configurable persisted warning in cron run logs and UI, a narrower log-only warning, or a deeper change to cron execution semantics?
rationale: The bug is real from source inspection, but the requested fix crosses config, protocol, persisted run-log, and UI boundaries where repository policy expects maintainer product/upgrade judgment.

options.title: Repair and land the linked warning PR
options.body: Keep the warning-based approach, but resolve conflicts and require upgrade-safe config/protocol/run-log proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow to log-only warning
options.body: Avoid new persisted/protocol/UI surface and emit only a structured gateway log warning, reducing compatibility scope at the cost of weaker operator visibility.

options.title: Change execution semantics
options.body: Make affected cron runs fail, skip, or await agent processing instead of warning after the fact, which may be more correct but has a higher behavior-change risk.

recommendation.title: Repair and land the linked warning PR
recommendation.body: Keep the warning-based approach, but resolve conflicts and require upgrade-safe config/protocol/run-log proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent cron/gateway persistence work and sampled line blame make this the best available routing candidate for the product/upgrade-shape decision.
